title: Minimax Point-Dose Mean Rates under Rough Covariates and Lipschitz Dose Dependence
banked_reason: D0.5.G assigned subfield below the field floor: paper score ceiling 7.3 < 7.4; fixed-tuple strengthened-class result, salvageable=false, with math and decision panels PASS.
gap_reasons: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope.

The delivered theorems establish matching n^(-4/19) MSE bounds for the fixed tuple and the specifically strengthened class P_star; they do not establish the broader anisotropic or slice-Hölder frontier, and the framing generally respects that boundary.

The fixed single smoothness tuple, absence of an implemented estimator or numerical verification, and limited public-comparator analysis keep the projected leading-journal score below the strongest matched-minimax papers.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved a matched n^(-4/19) minimax MSE rate without a logarithmic loss on the specified rough-covariate class P_star, using an observable multiscale estimator and an all-estimator correlated-sign lower bound. Both typed D0.5 panels passed with no findings, but the general panel graded the single-tuple result subfield under the required field floor. The broader anisotropic and slice-Hölder frontier remains open; formalization did not begin.
tldr: For the interior point-dose mean under eight Hölder-\(1/4\) covariates and Lipschitz dose dependence, an explicit split-sample multiscale Taylor estimator and a normalized correlated-sign experiment establish \(\mathsf R_n\asymp n^{-4/19}\) without a logarithmic factor on \(\mathcal P_\star\). At the aligned tuple \((d,s,\alpha,\beta)=(8,1/4,1,1)\), the accepted artifact \(\texttt{stat\_dose\_response\_minimax/holder\_anisotropic\_converse}\) supplies only the all-\(\beta\) fixed-baseline-propensity oracle lower floor \(n^{-2/3}\) and leaves the rough-covariate same-class upper frontier open. The present matched theorem is a strict advance on the concrete class \(\mathcal P_\star\), but it does not claim to close the accepted artifact's broader slice-Hölder class.
gap: The closest point-dose paper proves conditional higher-order risk bounds but does not supply an unconditional minimax theorem on this rough full law class. The existing internal converse gives the candidate exponent, while its upper estimator applies only on a smaller region and its fine empirical Gram route is singular here.
fill: The proposal rationalizes the estimand as \(\int uv/w\), inverts only a coarse positive pilot, estimates nested quadratic details with resolution-dependent bandwidths, adds one coarse cubic correction, and matches this upper construction to a legal normalized joint-nuisance mixture.
